bugs.title: Shadow Clone creation stalls forever on 'Preparing repository…'
bugs.notes: Seeded 2026-08-28. Live user-facing failure: progress message stuck at first indeterminate stage, no success/error ever shown; /start works afterwards (flow died silently). Prior sweep (bug-47/48) claimed a fix + live verification but symptom persists post-sweep, and bug-63 apparently moved the copy to a dispatched Actions workflow with polling of .clipforge-clone-status.json — investigate from current code: (1) can createPrivateShadowClone reject unhandled / escape try-catch in handleClonePatMessage (onProgress throw, Promise.all rejection, Worker kill on CPU/wall-clock limit); (2) is the whole op exceeding Workers request duration (600+ sequential API calls at chunk 4) — if so, structural redesign to workflow_dispatch relay pattern (check whether bug-63 already did this and where the stall actually is, e.g. polling loop never resolving); (3) can renderInteractiveView/onProgress edit calls throw 429 uncaught. Regardless of root cause: every clone attempt must end in success OR a clear error message — never silent stall. Verify end-to-end vs live GitHub API with realistic-size repo. [in_progress 2026-08-28] Beginning investigation: reading bot/src/github.js createPrivateShadowClone, bot/src/index.js handleClonePatMessage, and the bug-63 async copy workflow + polling loop to find where the stall lives. [done 2026-08-28] ROOT CAUSE (from current code, not prior notes): bug-63 moved the bulk copy into a dispatched Actions workflow, but the WEBHOOK handler still awaited the copy-status poll loop inline for up to CLONE_COPY_DEADLINE_MS (10 min). Cloudflare kills long-lived Workers invocations (the wrangler config has no duration-budget binding, so the default per-request budget applies and is not contractually guaranteed), and a kill is not a rejection — no catch in handleClonePatMessage or the outer handleUpdate can run, so neither the success message nor the error message was ever sent and onProgress edits stopped at the first indeterminate stage. That is exactly the reported symptom (frozen at "Preparing repository…", then /start works). The bug-47/48 sweep missed this because its tests asserted on createPrivateShadowClone's return/throw, never on the Worker being killed before either path ran. FIX (structural, commit a5037b7): (1) fetch() acks Telegram immediately and routes updates via ctx.waitUntil; (2) createPrivateShadowClone split into beginShadowCloneCreation (webhook: repo create + bootstrap + dispatch + ≤30s inline fast-path), pollShadowCloneJob (one read/tick with start/stall/deadline guards), finalizeShadowClone (PAT tail: workflow files, one-time-workflow cleanup, branch normalize, tree verify), cancelShadowCloneRun; (3) long copies are staged as an AES-GCM-encrypted KV clone job and resumed by a NEW cron trigger (scheduled() + "triggers":{"crons":["* * * * *"]} in wrangler.bot-a.jsonc); every staged job is guaranteed to end in a success or clearly-worded error message, failed creations best-effort delete the incomplete repo, and finalize throws retry each tick until the deadline then fail loudly. VERIFIED: node --check on all touched files; full bot suite 119/119 including 9 new clone-jobs tests that pin the KV round-trip (PAT re-encrypted, scan-set index) and every pollShadowCloneJob transition. Tests caught two real bugs I then fixed: getCloneJob threw (killing the cron tick) on an undecryptable envelope instead of returning null, and the deadline check was unreachable while a status file existed. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: no repo-capable PAT is present in this sandbox, so an end-to-end creation against the real GitHub API could not be run here — that confidence rests on the unchanged bug-63 workflow YAML (untouched), the preserved API sequence in begin/finalize, and the unit-level state-machine coverage. Deploy requires the Deploy Bots workflow to pick up the new cron trigger (triggers section) — first deploy of this commit also arms the cron.

bugs.title: Shadow Clones should relay through central Bot A/Bot B, not need their own
bugs.notes: Seeded 2026-08-28. Architecture change. Clones currently lack the direct-video Telegram relay (INTERNAL_RELAY_GROUP_CHAT_ID/RELAY_ENCRYPTION_KEY exist only on central Worker; isOriginalRepo gates in bot/src/index.js). Goal: a clone hands the relay step off to central Bot A/Bot B via an authenticated, per-clone-scoped API/webhook/dispatch — central secrets must NOT be copied to clones. Must preserve sealed-payload security model (bot/src/relay.js; tests: sealed-payload, relay caption, rememberCopiedMedia) multi-tenant: Bot B only acts on payloads matching a job it was told to expect. Audit all 7 isOriginalRepo call sites; touch only relay-related gating. Extend test/*.mjs relay suite. Document design in code comments like the rest of the codebase. Do not rush. [in_progress 2026-08-28] bug-51 done+confirmed on origin/main (a5037b7). Beginning bug-52: auditing all isOriginalRepo call sites in bot/src/index.js, then reading bot/src/relay.js, bot/src/relay-worker.js, handleRelayVideo + confirm-time relay dispatch, and the sealed-payload tests to map the current security model before designing the cross-repo relay handoff. [done 2026-08-28] AUDIT RESULT (from current code + ARCHITECTURE.md, not the bug's premise): the requested architecture ALREADY EXISTS. §10: "One shared Bot A deployment serves all users. Each private Telegram chat is bound to exactly one GitHub repo (that user's clone)." Shadow Clones are GitHub REPOSITORIES — they do not run their own Worker or BOT_TOKEN, so "a clone needs its own Bot A/Bot B pair" can never happen: every clone owner's chat is served by the central Bot A Worker, which holds INTERNAL_RELAY_GROUP_CHAT_ID (public var in wrangler.bot-a.jsonc, so "not configured yet" cannot fire) and RELAY_ENCRYPTION_KEY (Worker secret). The relay path (handleWizardRelayVideo → startRelayJob → Bot B → central telegram-relay.yml) has NO isOriginalRepo gate: audited all 7 call sites — 501/559 gate telegram_channel (§9.1), 1811/1823/2195 gate the news broadcast, 2037 gates push-update, 1864 is settings-button visibility for those same controls, start.js:173 is the home-screen auto-sync guard. NONE touch telegram_relay. The §9.2 sealed envelope already carries target_repo + the user's own PAT with the workflow's handoff_token substitution, so the central workflow writes into the OWNING user's clone — multi-tenant by design, matching §9.2's own text ("lets any user (including clone owners)…"). The stale wrangler.bot-a.jsonc comment "(used when the relay phase lands)" was misleading but harmless. NO isOriginalRepo gate was relaxed: relaxing one would have WEAKENED the §9.1 security boundary. WHAT WAS ADDED (commit 226555a): (1) 3 new tests in the EXISTING relay suite pinning the multi-tenant isolation guarantee (same-group two-tenant isolation of media + sealed payload; identical job ids across chats cannot alias because KV keys are per-chat; Bot B relevance gate is deliberately tenant-agnostic since tenancy = per-chat KV key + message-id-matched payload); (2) a relay.js header comment documenting the cross-repo model for future stateless agents. Full suite 122/122. CAVEAT: the sealed-payload tests cover the Bot A/Bot B handoff contract; relay/telegram_relay.py's in-workflow handling was not re-audited line-by-line (preserved subsystem, untouched by this change).

bugs.title: Clone Deploy Bots fails: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN never provisioned
bugs.notes: Seeded 2026-08-28. Real Actions log on fresh clone (clipforge-clone-zuaua5): wrangler deploy fails for missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; bug-68 failure-alert step then ALSO fails (exit 1) because BOTB_MTPROTO_BOT_TOKEN absent. Fix: (a) bot/setup flow must tell user exactly which secrets to add and where (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions), matching bug-53 docs; (b) consider optional Cloudflare-token collection in create-clone flow with setActionsSecret provisioning (check whether ANY secret provisioning already happens in createPrivateShadowClone) — documented manual step is acceptable if auto-provisioning is a large scope increase; (c) verify announceDeployFailure polling (bot/src/commands/start.js) works cross-repo for clones; (d) make the intentional-failure alert step clearer in Actions UI (e.g. ::error:: annotation) so a red X is distinguishable from a broken alert. [in_progress 2026-08-28] bug-53 done+confirmed (8743550). Starting bug-54: checking (a) where clone setup/settings surfaces required-secrets guidance, (b) whether createPrivateShadowClone/beginShadowCloneCreation already provisions ANY Actions secret via setActionsSecret, (c) announceDeployFailure cross-repo behavior (bot/src/commands/start.js), and (d) the deploy-bots.yml bug-68 alert step (add ::error:: annotation for a clearer Actions-UI failure signal). [done 2026-08-28] FIXED (commit 4f1328d). (a) SETUP GUIDANCE SURFACED: the GitHub clone settings screen (bot/src/index.js, the set:github menu a connected clone owner actually visits) now shows an explicit "Required setup" note naming CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and the exact location (repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions), matching bug-53's README section; shown only for connected non-original repos, main-owner chats untouched. (b) AUTO-PROVISIONING DECISION: verified beginShadowCloneCreation and the whole clone path provision NO Actions secrets today (only GEMINI_API_KEYS/ZERNIO_API_KEY are ever written, from their own settings screens via updateActionsSecret). Collecting a Cloudflare token during onboarding would require a new secure-input flow + validation + storage decision — a real scope increase the bug explicitly allows deferring; the documented manual step (README) + in-bot hint is the resolution. (c) announceDeployFailure VERIFIED CROSS-REPO BY CONSTRUCTION: bot/src/commands/start.js polls listWorkflowRuns(credentials, credentials.repo, deploy-bots.yml) with the OWNER'S PAT on the home-screen touchpoint, gated to non-original repos only — it is wired for clones, not the central repo, exactly as bug-68 intended. No change needed. (d) ALERT STEP CLARITY: the bug-68 intentional-failure branch in deploy-bots.yml now emits a ::error:: annotation ("Deploy blocked on a Shadow Clone") explaining the missing CLOUDFLARE_* secrets and the deliberate failure, so the run summary page itself explains the red X instead of it only being explained in a shell comment. VERIFIED: node --check on index.js, YAML parse of deploy-bots.yml, full bot suite 122/122.
